Scene imports and renders kit primitives, and Stage mounts the active Scene.

subcomponents.title: Preview addressing and runtime/step error detection

criteria.rationale: The verifier reserves a port on 127.0.0.1 and uses that same host for preview binding, readiness fetches, and the browser URL.
evidence: freePort listens on the host constant; preview receives --host host; fetch and page.goto use the resulting URL.

criteria.rationale: Readiness checks the child exit code only before fetch. A stale responder can satisfy the fetch if the intended child exits while that request is pending; the verifier does not confirm ownership after the response or fail on a later child exit.
evidence: The readiness loop checks preview.child.exitCode, then awaits fetch(url), and accepts an OK response without another child check.

criteria.rationale: The verifier collects both console and page errors, but focused executable evidence covers only console.error. No cited test injects an uncaught page error and asserts its nonzero, step identified outcome.
evidence: The browser-error and step-three-error faults inject console.error; neither injects a pageerror.
The pageerror listener exists, but its failure path lacks the required focused regression.

criteria.rationale: A focused fault test injects an error on step three and asserts a nonzero result, the step-three failure phase, and a console error attributed only to step three. It also tests a broken transition.
evidence: The step-three-error fixture injects console.error when through === 2 and checks the reported step.
The transition fixture disables next navigation and asserts a step-two failure.

subcomponents.title: Complete, settled screenshot capture

criteria.rationale: The helper captures each reported step in its navigation loop. A two-step fixture invokes the local inspect command and asserts that both numbered PNG files were produced with content.
evidence: The helper navigates to the requested slug on its preview URL, iterates over data-step-count, screenshots each index, and advances to the next index.
The fixture test reads and checks both step-01.png and step-02.png.

criteria.rationale: Capture uses a fixed 950 ms wait. It neither observes animation completion nor uses a transition contract consumed by persistent scene motion.
evidence: Each screenshot follows page.waitForTimeout(950).
The stage and scene motion define their own transitions; the helper does not observe their completion.

demo-integration.rationale: Talk delegates orchestration to the shared Presentation component. Its shared Scene composes the kit's Box, Arrow, Label, SymbolChip, and Frame primitives; Presentation delegates scene mounting to Stage. The delivered scene does not duplicate those shared mechanisms.
evidence: Talk renders <Presentation steps={STEPS}>.
Scene imports and renders kit primitives, and Stage mounts the active Scene.

demo-integration.rationale: The nine outline entries are mapped to one Scene function and one groupKey. Stage uses that groupKey for both LayoutGroup and the keyed scene wrapper, so adjacent steps keep the grouped mount. Separately, Scene passes presentation-owned ENTITY values as entityId; each used node primitive assigns that value to its motion layoutId and DOM entity hook.
evidence: STEPS maps every outline entry to groupKey 'how-to-evolving-scene' and the same Scene.
ENTITY.you and ENTITY.prompt persist from the first step; later nodes and cards retain their own ENTITY values after introduction.
Box, Arrow, Label, SymbolChip, and Frame consume entityId as layoutId.

demo-integration.rationale: The required public title is supplied by Talk, passed through Presentation, and rendered by Header in browse mode. The delivered initialMode, steps, groupKey, and entity IDs also reach their respective navigation, stage, and node consumers.
evidence: Talk supplies the title and initialMode props.
Presentation forwards title to Header and steps to Stage; Header renders title.
Stage consumes groupKey; node primitives consume entityId.

demo-integration.rationale: Footer progress buttons and Toc entries expose semantic current state plus a stable active-state attribute. Presentation-local CSS targets those attributes. The default attribution link is implemented in the project-local Presentation component and styled by presentation-local CSS.
evidence: Footer uses aria-current='step' and data-presentation-active; Toc uses aria-current='location' and the same active hook.
The local stylesheet gives active progress and Toc controls distinct rules and styles the attribution hook.
Presentation renders the default 'made by and-scene' link to the project repository.

demo-integration.rationale: The registry only registers and loads the talk. Talk owns the delivered title, step selection, and stylesheet; its local outline, entities, Scene, and CSS hold the demo-specific content and treatment. The shared Presentation boundary consumes generic steps and props without a demo-specific branch.
evidence: The registry contains a route and lazy loader for the talk.
The presentation-local files contain the outline, entity IDs, scene state, and styling.
Presentation renders generic steps, chrome, and attribution without referencing this demo.

demo-integration.rationale: All nine outline entries update the payload of one grouped Scene. Its threshold conditions retain earlier objects as steps advance: you and prompt persist throughout; conversation, skill, and question persist after step two; cards retain their indexed ENTITY IDs as they accumulate; later kit, verify, modify, and reveal objects remain after introduction. Stage keeps the scene wrapper keyed by the common groupKey, while kit nodes carry the separate ENTITY identities as layoutId values.
evidence: STEPS derives nine payload values from the nine-entry outline and assigns the same Scene and groupKey.
Scene uses cumulative through thresholds and stable ENTITY values for its semantic objects.
Stage keys the scene by groupKey; node primitives assign entityId to layoutId and data-presentation-entity.

scene-kit.rationale: Each step carries an ID and narration fields, and the authored steps supply them.
evidence: StepMeta requires id, era, title, and caption; STEPS maps the nine outline entries into scene steps.

scene-kit.rationale: Displayed step numbers come from the active array index.
evidence: Footer renders index + 1 in the present title, browse counter, and progress labels.

scene-kit.rationale: The step and scene share a generic payload type, which Stage passes to the active scene.
evidence: Step<TPayload> binds SceneProps<TPayload> to payload: TPayload; Stage renders Scene with step.payload.

scene-kit.rationale: Persisting entities have stable identities and an implemented layout animation path.
evidence: Box renders a motion element with layout and layoutId={entityId}; grouped Stage renders keep the same scene key across steps.

scene-kit.rationale: Newcomer entry uses a fixed delay that is not tied to the continuing entities' layout settlement.
evidence: Appear uses ENTER_DELAY, while Box's layout animation does not consume LAYOUT_T or provide a completion signal. The sample adds entities conditionally without Appear.

scene-kit.rationale: The scene boundary retains an exiting scene, but does not retain an ordinary entity removed conditionally inside a continuing grouped scene.
evidence: Stage's AnimatePresence wraps the keyed scene only; Scene conditionally renders child entities directly, with no child exit boundary.

scene-kit.rationale: Steps in the authored group update the same mounted scene with a new payload.
evidence: STEPS assigns one groupKey and Scene function to every step; Stage keys the scene by groupKey and passes the current payload.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped scene and its continuing child elements stay mounted as payload changes, so their initial state is not replayed.
evidence: Stage retains the same keyed Scene; Scene renders the continuing 'you' and prompt entities at stable positions with stable entity IDs.

scene-kit.rationale: The authored group explicitly composes persistent nodes and staged additions in one scene.
evidence: Scene uses payload.through to retain the conversation and progressively add cards, connectors, verification, revision, and reveal elements at authored positions.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode keeps the active step title while removing browse reading chrome.
evidence: Footer renders the numbered active title in present mode; Header hides its browse title, and Presentation omits the table of contents.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode supplies the active title and wrapping caption, table of contents, controls, and progress indicators.
evidence: Footer renders title, caption, progress buttons, and previous/next buttons; Presentation renders Toc in browse mode; caption CSS permits multiple lines.

scene-kit.rationale: Mode changes update only mode state, leaving the step index intact.
evidence: toggleMode calls setMode without setIndex; the focused runtime test jumps to index 2 and asserts index 2 after both toggles.

scene-kit.rationale: Supported navigation keys advance or reverse the clamped index.
evidence: The key handler maps ArrowRight, Space, and PageDown to next, and ArrowLeft and PageUp to prev; the runtime test exercises arrow navigation.

scene-kit.rationale: The handler checks horizontal predominance but does not reject multi-touch gestures, and there are no focused vertical and multi-touch assertions.
evidence: onTouchStart records only touches[0] coordinates; onTouchEnd uses changedTouches[0] without checking touch count.

scene-kit.rationale: Progress and section controls call the direct index setter.
evidence: Footer progress buttons and Toc buttons call onJump; Presentation binds onJump to nav.go, and the runtime test clicks a progress item and asserts index 2.

scene-kit.rationale: The active progress item and section have semantic current-state attributes and stable active hooks.
evidence: Footer sets aria-current='step' and data-presentation-active; Toc sets aria-current='location' and the same active hook based on the current era.

scene-kit.rationale: Presentation keyboard navigation leaves focused controls' key handling alone.
evidence: The key handler returns for buttons, links, and form controls; the runtime test focuses Next, presses ArrowLeft, and asserts the step index stays at 2.

scene-kit.rationale: Reverse navigation cannot move below index zero.
evidence: clamp bounds indices at zero; the runtime test presses ArrowLeft at the first step and asserts index 0 and a disabled Previous button.

scene-kit.rationale: Forward navigation cannot move beyond the final step.
evidence: clamp bounds indices at count - 1; the runtime test presses ArrowRight and PageDown at the end and asserts the last index and a disabled Next button.

scene-kit.rationale: The fit uses window allowances rather than the stage's actual available height, so the canvas can exceed the stage at an ordinary viewport.
evidence: source audit: useFitScale.ts subtracts 60 + 92 pixels in present mode. At a 1280×532 viewport it selects scale 1 for the 380-pixel canvas; src/index.css gives the header a 62-pixel minimum and footer…

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered stage defaults to the approved 880×380 authored canvas.
evidence: DESIGN_W and DESIGN_H are 880 and 380; Stage consumes them as its default width and height.

scene-kit.rationale: Kit markup exposes stable classes and data attributes for presentation styling.
evidence: Presentation, Stage, Footer, and Box render named class and data hooks; the authored stylesheet targets those hooks.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit supplies semantic structure and hooks without a kit-owned color or typography theme.
evidence: The kit's rendered elements provide class hooks and motion/layout properties; the focused source test checks every kit file for visual defaults, and presentation-owned CSS supplies the sample&#39…

scene-kit.rationale: The kit operates without a required CSS framework.
evidence: Package dependencies contain React and motion but no styling framework; the authored presentation uses ordinary CSS, and the kit source test checks for Tailwind dependencies and tokens.

scene-kit.rationale: Kit entities accept authored style and class props, allowing coordinate-based diagrams.
evidence: Box spreads motion div props including style and className; the sample supplies per-card left/top coordinates and uses positioned CSS for scene entities.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit renders the default link, but its bottom-right position comes from host-owned CSS rather than the kit.
evidence: Presentation renders the default attribution anchor without positioning; src/index.css supplies .presentation-attribution { position: absolute; right: 18px; bottom: 8px; }, while the bootstrap host s…

scene-kit.rationale: The attribution anchor has stable selectors for host or presentation CSS.
evidence: Presentation renders className='presentation-attribution' and data-presentation-attribution on the anchor; the authored stylesheet targets its class.

scene-kit.rationale: No top-left brand is supplied by default, and callers can explicitly provide one.
evidence: Presentation accepts optional brand and passes it to Header; Header renders only that value in the brand slot, and the authored Talk omits the prop.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires asking only for missing information, one question at a time.
evidence: Section 1 states: “Ask only for information that is missing, one question at a time.”

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill permits proceeding when the user chooses to supply partial details and directs the agent to make reversible decisions for open choices.
evidence: Section 1 says a user may explicitly proceed with partial details and specifies how to handle open choices.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill directs the agent to proceed without redundant questions when topic, style, and steps are supplied.
evidence: Section 1 explicitly covers a request that already supplies topic, style, and steps.

presentation-skill.rationale: The focused bootstrap test copies the complete template into a new temporary app, installs dependencies there, builds it, and verifies a rendered route.
evidence: The bootstrap test creates a temporary app path, copies templates/bootstrap into it, runs npm ci and build from that path, then asserts a passing browser render check.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill instructs reuse of existing anchors, but no focused scaffold test constructs a target with all anchors present and verifies reuse without replacement.
evidence: The bootstrap test starts from a fresh copied template; it does not exercise an already scaffolded target.

presentation-skill.rationale: No focused executable evidence constructs a target with some anchors present and verifies that only missing infrastructure is added.
evidence: The scaffold policy describes preserving valid anchors, while the bootstrap test only copies the complete template into a new app.

presentation-skill.rationale: The scaffolded kit is checked against the canonical kit, and focused assertions reject visual defaults and Tailwind dependencies.
evidence: The bootstrap test compares every scaffolded kit file with the canonical kit and checks scaffold CSS and dependencies for theme defaults; the kit contract test checks that kit source contains no CSS …

presentation-skill.rationale: The bootstrap test resolves the template from a source-file-anchored skill directory and installs dependencies from the materialized app target.
evidence: The test derives skillRoot from import.meta.url, copies templates/bootstrap from that root, and invokes npm ci with the materialized app as cwd.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill specifies a presentations app location, but no focused test constructs a monorepo and verifies the selected target and resulting files.
evidence: The bootstrap test uses a single temporary app path and supplies no workspace declaration, apps layout, or packages layout.

presentation-skill.rationale: The fresh-app test covers an empty target, but no focused evidence constructs an existing standalone target and verifies root selection and its specific scaffold outcome.
evidence: The bootstrap test copies a complete template into a new app rather than detecting and scaffolding an existing standalone project.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy requires confirmation for a nonempty unscaffolded target, but no focused executable test or workflow record exercises that branch and verifies that writing waits for a choice.
evidence: The bootstrap test merely checks that SKILL.md contains the phrase “non-empty, unscaffolded target”; its setup is a new app and has no confirmation branch.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires a new folder and registry entry, and the implemented router resolves that registry entry to a lazily loaded presentation.
evidence: Section 3 requires one explicit registry entry; presentations is an explicit slug-to-loader array, and main.tsx selects the matching slug and renders its loaded component.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill assigns visual styling to presentation-owned CSS, and the shipped presentation imports its own style sheet while the kit contract test rejects kit visual defaults.
evidence: Section 3 assigns styling to presentation-owned CSS; Talk.tsx imports ./style.css, which defines the presentation and scene styles; the kit contract test checks for absent kit CSS and visual defaults.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires leaving existing presentations and routes intact when creating a presentation and preserving unrelated presentations during modification.
evidence: Section 3 states both preservation requirements; the registry is an array of independent entries, allowing a new entry without replacing existing ones.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires identifying the modification target and asking the user to choose when it is missing or ambiguous.
evidence: Section 1 directs the agent to list available presentations and ask which one before editing an ambiguous target.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly confines modification to the selected presentation and directly required registry or host files.
evidence: Section 3 states the edit scope and requires preserving unrelated presentations.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill makes build, browser render and navigation, and settled browser inspection checks prerequisites to reporting completion.
evidence: Section 4 requires build, real-browser route and navigation checks, and inspection of representative settled views before completion.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires repairing failed checks and rerunning build, render, and inspection before reporting success.
evidence: Section 4 says to fix failed checks and rerun checks after fixes; Section 5 permits a success report only after required failures are fixed.

verification-tooling.rationale: The verifier reads the canonical outline before building. A missing file rejects into the catch block, which sets a nonzero exit code.
evidence: The outline read is inside the verifier's try/catch; the catch sets process.exitCode to 1.
The missing-sample fault test deletes outline.json and asserts a nonzero result.

verification-tooling.rationale: The verifier reserves a port on 127.0.0.1 and uses that same host for preview binding, readiness fetches, and the browser URL.
evidence: freePort listens on the host constant; preview receives --host host; fetch and page.goto use the resulting URL.

verification-tooling.rationale: Readiness checks the child exit code only before fetch. A stale responder can satisfy the fetch if the intended child exits while that request is pending; the verifier does not confirm ownership after the response or fail on a later child exit.
evidence: The readiness loop checks preview.child.exitCode, then awaits fetch(url), and accepts an OK response without another child check.

verification-tooling.rationale: The verifier collects both console and page errors, but focused executable evidence covers only console.error. No cited test injects an uncaught page error and asserts its nonzero, step identified outcome.
evidence: The browser-error and step-three-error faults inject console.error; neither injects a pageerror.
The pageerror listener exists, but its failure path lacks the required focused regression.

verification-tooling.rationale: A focused fault test injects an error on step three and asserts a nonzero result, the step-three failure phase, and a console error attributed only to step three. It also tests a broken transition.
evidence: The step-three-error fixture injects console.error when through === 2 and checks the reported step.
The transition fixture disables next navigation and asserts a step-two failure.

verification-tooling.rationale: The project exposes a separate local inspect command that builds, opens a preview in Playwright, and writes step screenshots.
evidence: The inspect script launches Chromium and saves step-numbered PNGs; package.json exposes it as npm run inspect.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper captures each reported step in its navigation loop. A two-step fixture invokes the local inspect command and asserts that both numbered PNG files were produced with content.
evidence: The helper navigates to the requested slug on its preview URL, iterates over data-step-count, screenshots each index, and advances to the next index.
The fixture test reads and checks both step-01.png and step-02.png.

verification-tooling.rationale: Capture uses a fixed 950 ms wait. It neither observes animation completion nor uses a transition contract consumed by persistent scene motion.
evidence: Each screenshot follows page.waitForTimeout(950).
The stage and scene motion define their own transitions; the helper does not observe their completion.

verification-tooling.rationale: The regression asserts only that some overlap warning appears. It does not identify the injected collision in its assertion or exercise representative nested text and chrome collisions, so the required focused evidence is incomplete.
evidence: The fixture places collision-alpha and collision-beta spans together, but its positive assertion matches only the generic warning phrase.
The helper scans text and chrome selectors, yet the test does not assert a warning naming the fixture collision.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper excludes every descendant of an allowed-overlap container from all collision comparisons, which can also hide collisions with unrelated elements. The test does not establish that the unmarked collision was reported.
evidence: source audit: scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs filters out elements matching element.closest(&#39;[data-allow-overlap]&#39;) before pairwise comparison.
source audit: tests/verification.integration.test.mjs checks for a generic warning and absence of the allowed pair, but never asserts a warning naming collision alpha and collision beta.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper compares computed styles of rendered active and inactive progress items. The fixture makes those styles identical and asserts the warning output.
evidence: The helper compares background, color, border, transform, and font weight using data-presentation-active selectors.
The fixture sets identical progress-button styles and asserts the indistinct-marker warning.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper inspects the rendered attribution's visibility and styling. A focused fixture gives it undersized, browser-default styling and asserts the corresponding warning.
evidence: The helper checks effective visibility, font size, color, and underline before emitting the attribution warning.
The fixture applies 8 px blue underlined attribution styling and asserts the warning.

testing-evidence.rationale: The final pass exercised the changed step-error attribution seam, but the packet does not show a substantial share of the approved user-visible behaviors being exercised. The earlier screenshot notes cover selected renders and generated routes, while navigation, modes, requirement gathering, scaffold variants, and several scene behaviors lack recorded public-surface exercises.
evidence: The round-1 exploration log records one controlled step-3 console-error exercise and explicitly says the earlier skill, scaffold, scene interaction, and visual journeys were not replayed.
The screenshot README describes selected rendered steps and routes but contains no recorded keyboard, swipe, mode-toggle, direct-jump, or requirement-gathering interaction.

testing-evidence.rationale: The step-3 diagnostic has a specific verified log, and the screenshot README records some visual observations. Material broader claims, including the listed kit contract coverage and generated-project behavior, lack equally specific verified action-and-result records; the screenshots themselves are marked defective for missing capture metadata.
evidence: The verified round-1 fault log reports: “FAIL [browser render step 3]: Browser render failed: step 3: console.error: AT-ROUND1 injected step three runtime fault”.
The assumptions ledger says `tests/kit.contract.test.mjs` covers navigation, modes, attribution, and other behaviors, but the packet has no corresponding test result.
The verified index marks every candidate screenshot defective with `missing-capture-metadata`.

testing-evidence.rationale: The recorded tested revision is the final revision. The verified round-1 record identifies the two changed files since its declared diff base and exercises their browser-error attribution seam with a controlled product-verifier run.
evidence: The tested-revision artifact records `f5bb0a0fd6381cb40d8e80873915e0561312bf0f`, matching the harness final SHA, with zero changes to final.
The exploration log identifies `scripts/verify.mjs` and `tests/verification.integration.test.mjs` as the diff and records the step-3-only fault reproduction and result.

testing-evidence.rationale: The record distinguishes the narrow final pass from historical coverage, identifies omitted checks and absent CI, and discloses unresolved issues and visual observations. Its readiness statement is qualified as readiness for human review, without claiming a full final-revision retest.
evidence: The final handoff says the round-0 journeys and visuals were not repeated, and lists the full suite, lint, other fault classes, and browser and viewport matrices as unexercised.
The exploration log records that no current-head CI run was found and that the draft review check was not CI evidence.
The assumptions ledger explicitly lists unresolved U1, U2, U3, U4, and U5; the screenshot README records visual observations and the before-and-after warning fixture.

assumption-handling.rationale: The ledger surfaces consequential questions about the test runner, phone scaling, outline source of truth, and scaffold verifier diagnostics. It also records the intermittent favicon observation with its evidence limit.
evidence: The assumptions ledger lists U1–U5 with observations, possible decisions, and impacts.

assumption-handling.rationale: The ledger acknowledges that the scaffold verifier reports browser errors without a failing step while the stated verification requirement calls for identifying that step. It classifies conformity as undecided without establishing that scaffolded verification is exempt.
evidence: U5 says the scaffold verifier reports `Browser errors at /<slug>: ...` with no step, yet describes aligning it with the root verifier as a decision rather than a required correction.

assumption-handling.rationale: The candidate presents accepting route-level scaffold diagnostics as an option despite the recorded step-identification requirement and the known diagnostic gap.
evidence: U5 offers either to bring the scaffold verifier into alignment or to “accept the generic route-level report for scaffolded projects.”

assumption-handling.rationale: The handoff omits U5 entirely, losing the scaffold diagnostic gap, its consequence for authors, and the proposed action.
evidence: The final handoff says four unresolved items remain and names only U1–U4; the ledger separately records U5.

demo-integration.rationale: Talk uses the shared Presentation boundary, which mounts the active scene through Stage. The shared Scene renders scene-kit primitives, and the supplied implementation shows no duplicated mounting or node mechanism.
evidence: Talk.tsx renders <Presentation steps={STEPS}>.

scene-kit.rationale: Stable entity IDs feed an implemented layout animation path within a retained grouped scene.
evidence: Box.tsx renders a motion element with layout and layoutId={entityId}; Stage.tsx keys the grouped scene by groupKey.

scene-kit.rationale: The continuing layout motion does not consume the newcomer delay or provide a completion signal; the authored newcomers do not use the delayed entry component.
evidence: Box.tsx supplies layout animation without LAYOUT_T; Appear.tsx uses fixed ENTER_DELAY; steps/index.tsx conditionally adds entities without Appear.

scene-kit.rationale: All authored steps use the same scene and group key while passing an updated payload.

scene-kit.rationale: The authored scene explicitly combines continuing entities with staged additions.

scene-kit.rationale: The key handler maps supported navigation keys to clamped movement, with focused arrow navigation exercised.

scene-kit.rationale: Forward navigation is bounded at the last index and exercised there.
